# tests/fixtures

Small WAVs `cargo test` decodes directly. Most of these carry speech and
have a reference transcript in `manifest.tsv` (see `tests/fixtures.rs`) —
this file only documents the ones that don't: fixtures with no reference
text because they are not supposed to transcribe to anything.

## `nonspeech-white.wav`, `nonspeech-rumble.wav`, `nonspeech-transient.wav`

**Synthetic — none of these is a real room recording.** Generated by
`bench/corpus/synthesize_nonspeech.sh` (ffmpeg `lavfi` noise sources; see
that script for the exact filter graph and amplitude for each). Added for
the Silero VAD gate work (mesa task 968): audio Parakeet is known to
hallucinate filler words on (a fan, a chair scrape, background hiss)
rather than return nothing, deliberately synthesized loud enough to clear
auris's existing energy gate (`src/audio.rs::is_silent`, max 30 ms-window
RMS below `SILENCE_RMS_THRESHOLD` = 1e-3) — a clip that gate already
rejects would prove nothing about VAD, since the recognizer would never be
reached either way.

Not in `manifest.tsv`: that file holds `id<TAB>reference transcript` pairs
for fixtures `tests/fixtures.rs` asserts a *specific* decoded transcript
against — these clips have no such reference by definition, since the
point is that they are meant to decode to nothing. `silence.wav` is the
existing precedent for a non-spoken fixture with no manifest entry.
`nonspeech-transient.wav` does not fully live up to that intent — see
below.

All three are 16 kHz mono 16-bit PCM, 4.00 s. Measured max 30 ms-window
RMS — the exact statistic `is_silent` computes, so this number is directly
comparable to `SILENCE_RMS_THRESHOLD`:

| file | generation | max-window RMS | vs. 1e-3 gate |
|---|---|---|---|
| `nonspeech-white.wav` | broadband white noise (`anoisesrc=color=white`, amplitude 0.065) | 0.040417 | 40x |
| `nonspeech-rumble.wav` | pink noise, lowpassed at 250 Hz — fan/HVAC proxy (amplitude 0.11) | 0.034720 | 35x |
| `nonspeech-transient.wav` | 150 ms filtered noise burst against silence — chair-scrape/knock proxy (amplitude 0.07) | 0.040754 | 41x |

All three sit in the 0.01-0.1 band mesa's browser-side onset gate (0.02)
actually passes through, so they exercise the same energy range a VAD gate
would see in practice, not an edge case near the threshold.

Regenerate with `bench/corpus/synthesize_nonspeech.sh` (idempotent;
`--force` to overwrite). See `bench/fixtures/README.md` for the related
`tts-nonspeech-case.wav` (a real-speech clip used as the opposite case —
what VAD should correctly classify as speech, not reject) and for
`bench/results/acoustic-wav/`, this repo's genuine room recordings.

### `nonspeech-transient.wav`: a known, unclosed gap

Of the three, this one is not actually rejected by the VAD gate
(`src/vad.rs`). Silero reports a confident ~0.55 s "speech" span in it at
every threshold measured, from 0.5 down to 0.05 — task 968's sweep found
no threshold that separates it from real speech, so this is not a tuning
gap, it is a Silero false positive on this specific synthetic burst.

Under the decision-not-filter design (`src/vad.rs`'s module doc comment),
a false positive here cannot corrupt anything — the gate either blocks the
recognizer or hands it the same, untouched clip `--no-vad` would have
decoded anyway. What that clip decodes *to* still depends on hotword
biasing: unbiased, the full 4 s clip happens to decode to nothing and
exits `NOTHING_TRANSCRIBED`; with `--vocabulary-file` (mesa's actual
production configuration), the same untouched clip decodes to a ~40-word
hallucinated string of boosted vocabulary terms. Both behaviors are
unchanged from pre-VAD auris — `is_silent` already let this clip through,
so this is not something task 968 introduced or made worse, only a
pre-existing gap it did not manage to close. Alternatives considered and
rejected: raising the detection threshold (fails at every value tested,
and would also reintroduce the false negative on `u17.wav` in
`bench/results/acoustic-wav/`), and a "reject short spans relative to clip
length" heuristic (would also reject genuinely short real utterances like
"yes" or "done" — speculative complexity for one synthetic fixture, not
attempted).
